correctness.rationale: An independent reconstruction from E and L reproduced 105x238 H_X,H_Z, row weight 8, exact CSS orthogonality, ranks 97/97 and k=44. Rebuilding the explicit support gave weight 6, zero H_Z syndrome, nonzero remainder modulo rowspace(H_X), and rank augmentation 97->98. Independent enumeration of the 16-dimensional kernel of the 21x35 base matrix gave minimum weight 6 with 21 such codewords. Exhaustive neighbourhood checks gave zero expansion failures at sizes 1,2,3 and exactly 84 at size 4. These facts directly falsify d>=9; no claim of exact quantum distance is needed.
residual_risks: The exact quantum minimum distance could be below six through other logical sectors; the record only claims the upper bound d<=6, which is fully supported.

source_inspections.trigger: Closest primary work on finite-length symmetric QC lifted-product distance design.

value.rationale: A concrete low-weight logical operator in a structured QC lifted-product code is a useful finite-length design obstruction: it invalidates a hoped-for distance-above-stabilizer certificate on a natural type-I protograph instance and pinpoints the associated local expansion failure. This is more than a normalization check and can guide selection of exponent arrays in the finite-length LP-QLDPC program.
residual_risks: The result is an obstruction for one structured instance, not a theorem about all 3x5 or lift-7 lifted-product codes.

final_claim: For the specified 3x5 quasi-cyclic base at lift 7, the symmetric lifted-product CSS code has N=238, rank(H_X)=rank(H_Z)=97 and k=44; the explicit weight-6 X operator on support {0,4,10,18,21,24} lies in ker(H_Z) but not rowspace(H_X), so d<=6 and the claimed d>=9 certificate is false; the base Tanner expansion also has exactly 84 failures at size four.
